paragraphs: BoodleBox sells a shared AI workspace where people and AI models work on the same material together. The company says it serves education, enterprise and individual users, and that higher education is where its design philosophy is most visible.

Shared workspaces let faculty, students and teams work together in real time rather than in separate private chat sessions. One account carries access to 38 AI models in a single workspace. Users can switch models mid-conversation and run the same prompt across several of them. Custom bots can be built on course materials, workflows and institutional knowledge.

The company says more than 120,000 educators, students and professionals have joined, along with hundreds of institutions and teams. It states SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, HIPAA and FERPA compliance. BoodleBox was founded by France Hoang. Hoang, a West Point graduate, named the company himself. The name comes from West Point, where boodle is what cadets call the cookies, cakes and treats sent from home.

quote.text: AI should make people more capable, not more dependent.
